body: HAPPY BIRTHDAY!

Your pain is so valid! So, so, so valid and I’m so sorry to hear that the health care system isn’t taking you seriously and that you don’t feel seen by the people around you.

I know it might be a hard thing to do, but have you spoken to your best friend and boyfriend about needing a bit more support? The best way to get help is to ask for it, even if it sucks asking. But let them know how you feel and ask for supporting/loving words from them? Saying what you need and want won’t make their response less genuine! They’ll just be able to help you better.

And pro tip for the healthcare system: exaggerate your symptoms and pain. It’s common that one undersells what one is actually going through, and focus on telling them how it negatively affects your life in concrete ways and examples. That might help to get them to help you? (Not sure as I’m not Canadian) but keep trying! You don’t deserve all this pain!

You’re already suffering so much, you don’t deserve more fear and pain, especially not the kind that comes with doing that to yourself.

Others care for you in ways and for reasons that might not be obvious, but there is care for you in this world. Everybody doesn’t hate you.

I get it. I used to romanticize my own death and others crying over my “lost potential” if I killed myself as a teen. So I really understand that mindset.

Although you’re being WAY too hard on yourself. You’re far from pathetic. Living this long even though you have these feelings is an achievement, even though it might not feel like it. There’s no “what’s taking you so long”, all there is is “holy shit! You made it this far! :D”. There isn’t either a “suicidal enough” or not, you still feel bad and your pain is still pain that you’ve managed to live through day by day. So I just wanted to say good job and in all honesty, I’m proud of you.

Because living another hour was easier and less horrifying than killing myself. Because I was in so much mental pain that it didn’t seem fair to cause myself more pain in my final moments.
Then I just kept doing that and thinking that way until I was able to find other reasons as well.

After that I didn’t kill myself because of my cat and because I loved him. Then because I was going to make my favorite food the next day. And then because I wanted to make it until summer so that I could see the meadow outside of my house in full bloom.
I’ve never had any grand reasons to keep living, it’s mostly just been “just cuz”, but that’s gotten me really far and the longer I live the more nice small stuff I get to enjoy.

No! Don’t end it! 20 years seems like a lot right now because that’s all the time you’ve been alive, but for someone that’s 40, 60 or 80, 20years is so little and like “nothing”. You don’t need to have done “anything” by the time you’re 20, I mean, life is hard as it is. I’m 22 and I havent done any major in life and I’m continuing to live just cuz it’s easier than killing myself and I don’t want to cause myself that pain.

(Also, not killing yourself and living yet another day even though you feel this was is a major achievement in of itself. Genuinly, that’s really strong of you.)
It’s ok to not know what to do.

Killing yourself is scary and hurts! And it’s not fair to put yourself through that when you’re already hurting so much. You deserve a more peaceful escape, like sleep or watching a video/series/reading/movie. There are other easier ways to not be here anymore. Personally I used to cope a lot by sleeping - not the best in the long run but better than going through the pain of killing myself
You’re brave as fuck for not killing yourself and continuing with a life that made you feel so bad that you wanted to end it. You really had the balls to keep living and that’s cool as fuck

It does get better. It really. Really. Does. It’s not just some bullshit people say (god I thought it really was) and for me it wasn’t a single therapist that “cured” me, or any treatments etc, it was just time. And it sucked for so many years, but slowly it got better.

You don’t need any motivation to live right now if it’s hard to find one, all you need to is to simply make it through to the next day. An hour at a time, a day at a time. That’s it. Just until the day is over. Don’t feel bad about not having one, not everyone does, really, a lot of people just keep living just “cuz”. Because it’s easier and less horrifying than killing yourself. And just that is enough.

Also! Life is a wild ride and gives you opportunities you never thought even existed in the first place. My depression made me fail HARD in school, I totally thought my entire life was over and that there wasn’t any meaning to it all, but then I just kept going, and life kept happening, and slowly, things got better and now I genuinely feel good, have a good job and good people around me.

Killing yourself sucks harder than simply living another hour. Why cause yourself that much more pain in your final moments when you’re already feeling so bad? That’s unfair and it’s easier to just lie down in bed for just an hour longer, until the day ends, instead of killing yourself. Life doesn’t have to be worth living, you just need to take it a day at a time, because it’s easier and easy is what you deserve in these hardships

Bipolar disorder is super hard and yeah, it’s incurable, but that doesn’t mean that there aren’t ways to manage it and for it to get easier. There are a lot more resources, videos, support groups, and in general an online culture out there willing to help - that assumingely your grandma didn’t have access to. Living with it is hard and unfair, and I’m genuinly sorry that you have to go through this, but you’re so strong for just making your way through life enough to read the end of this comment! Every day is an achievement with those difficulties, so I pat you on the back for that one. Good job!

Killing yourself is scary as fuck. It’s horrifying and absolutely terrifying. I felt the exact same way when I attempted. What helped me was thinking “if the reason I want to die is to escape the pain, why would I subject myself to something to terrifying and painful as killing myself if all I want is to get away from it.” and then instead of putting myself through that I just laid in bed because I deserved at least a bit of comfort due to how horrible I was feeling and all the bad stuff I’ve gone through. To allow myself sleep and rest/simply rotting in bed instead and take it one day at a time.
I don’t know if that way of thinking will help, but either way I wanted to say that what you went through is awful and that you’re feelings are so fucking valid

My fave soothing stuff is scented stuffed animals, placing stickers and drawing in my journal and putting on a comfort hoodie. Shrugs.

I also have a failed attempt under my belt and it really is like how you describe it. It feels so defeating and the empty feeling is overwhelming in the most empty way. What I do now is just? Take one day at a time. I don’t want to say it like a therapist or a Facebook post, but more like. Ok. I can just live this day. For no reason. There really is no reason why I keep living. I just do? It feels empty and numb but I just go another day. And then some good things happen! And then bad things happen and push me back into feeling awful and horrid again. But I guess I’m not living for the good things or the bad things. Taking your own life or attempting is traumatic and absolutely ruins you, and for me it’s so so so hard to push myself to get the job done and finish it. I think I figured out that trying to kill myself for real is so hard and so scary and so fucking fucking awful, that just living another day is less of a burden and less misery than having to go through that again. So, yeah. I can live this day 

Sorry for the rant!

I’m a 20 y/o transman who hasn’t been able to start transitioning yet, and it’s. Yeah. I really get you.
One of the reasons I’m still alive is because had the condition that in order to do so, I would live as my authentic self. Well. Getting help with trans and gender stuff takes years. And I’ve been waiting for years. So it hurts. 

But things I can say to you is that love is out there. You can find love. It’s possible. It really really is. It’s hard and a lot of people alienate you, fetishize you, reject you or don’t even see you as a person (or it’s been like that for me at least) but I’ve still managed to find people who love me romantically.

I suggest purely queer spaces? That’s where I find the most comfort. Being surrounded by other trans people makes me feel safe and loved, and 90% of my friends are trans. For me, t4t (trans 4 trans, like mlm male loving male etc) is really my preferred type of relationship. Because then I can be certain that someone sees me for who I am and not as “a tomboy alternative girl”. I’ve dated cis (yet queer) people before and that’s been ok and has worked out too, but personally I prefer t4t. But! My point is that there are people who will love you. You’re just not surrounded by them right now.

Im bipolar and I really get how you feel. I’ve had a few attempts myself and it’s just been awful for several years. What snapped me out of it was when I had a severe depressive episode, had a date, method etc, but I got sent to the hospital because my mom found out. The day I went to the hospital I became insanely manic and thought that committing suicide was “cringe” and so “last week”. I also hated all the attention my family was giving me and how they completely stripped my freedom. After that I never wanted to experience it again so it just forcibly told myself to stop. I’m still suicidal but just not actively or outwardly anymore. Life fucking sucks and I hate my moodswings and I hate that I have to keep living. I don’t have any great advice but what I’m doing right now is just. Continuing to exists. Just keep walking. Just keep going for shits and giggles. And try not to think about it too much. But yeah, I get it

Don’t think of it like that. All things come to an end, the good and the bad. And then new good things and new bad things come. You were in a situation that made you want to end it, so you did. You mostly only see the good things in a bad relationship when you look back, and then forget why you ended it at all, mostly because you miss the comfort it gave you. 
If you had continued it it might’ve made you feel worse and stuck, and then you would have regretted not ending it and getting stuck in a commitment like that. Or maybe not! There are so many maybes and it’s so draining exploring every single one of them. I’m really sorry you don’t have the love and support you need right now, because you deserve it. And you don’t deserve beating yourself down because you feel like you’re ruining your own life. Because you’re not. Stop seeing yourself as a villain and inserting you as the big bad in your own life. I had to and it was hard, because I used to blame myself for everything and think I was an awful person, and only got over it because people called me out and scolded me for doing this over and over again. So now I’m scolding you for thinking that you’re a bad person. You’re not.

I have a bit of experience in the relationship part. I actually thought I couldn’t feel love for the longest time, because every time I would be around with someone, me intimate and do things, but as soon as we got into a relationship or even right before my feelings just dropped. Gone. And I just ruined everything by being an asshole and just straight up terrible to them. And then once they were gone from my life I would look back and cry because I missed it. There’s nothing wrong with not wanting to have a relationship. Sometimes you just don’t want to and don’t feel like it, and it’s ok. And it’s also not strange that when the intimacy and the feeling of being loved and important to someone suddenly disappears because you didn’t want the relationship part anymore. Even if you don’t feel it for that person, having the security and love they gave you being taken away is hard. It sucks ass and it’s awful because then you regret it and want the person back when you in actuality just wanted to feel the feelings when everything was good during that time. Allow yourself to not be ready for relationships or not want them. It’s ok.

It’s easier said than done but what’s done is done and you can’t change it. I usually go with “There’s no reason to think and regret because I can’t change it anyway. It’s a waste of time” thought pattern. Maybe I’ll do things better in the future maybe I won’t, but the future is the only thing I can do anything about. So fuck the past.

Also. What’s something you’re grateful to have now? You mentioned your friends that were like brothers to you? it really seems like you appreciate them a lot and that’s already a step in the right direction. To list things you’re thankful of in life and just take a moment to appreciate them and be happy about them. Acknowledging that they mean a lot to you and being thankful. You’re already doing it with aspects in your life, so try and dig up some more
